title: CI never runs lore check, so the repo's stated docs gate has never gated — and it is red on dev right now
summary: The fleet operating rule is 'lore check exiting 0 is the definition of done for a docs change', but no job in .github/workflows runs it. Measured on dev at effd5dea: lore check exits 6. Cause: LCLI-333 carries status 'Blocked', which is outside quest's configured status flow (To Do / In Progress / Done, paused: Paused). It is the only off-flow record of 437. A gate nothing runs is a gate that silently stopped gating.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A CI job runs lore check on every PR and its exit code gates the merge
LCLI-333's off-flow status is resolved — either moved into the configured flow, or given a [reconcile.overrides] entry in .lore/config.toml with the reason recorded
The new job is added to dev's required status checks, matched by rendered job name verified by codepoint, so it actually blocks rather than merely reporting

implementationNotes:
Cross-reference: opum-agent OPAG-146 is the fleet-wide form of this finding. Orchestrator measured by ref on origin/dev at 2026-09-15T14:34Z: only opum-agent and opum-doc run lore check in CI; lore-cli and seven other repos carry .lore/config.toml and no lore check job. LCLI-504 stays lore-cli's half and is worked here, not in OPAG-146.

Re-measured locally on chore/LCLI-503-file-three-findings at 455407d6: 'lore check' exits 6 (78 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, 9 out-of-bundle links skipped, then the reconcile status error on LCLI-333's off-flow 'Blocked' status). Independently confirms the summary's dev measurement at effd5dea and shows the branch has not changed it. 'git grep -rn "lore check" .github/workflows/' returns nothing, so AC#1 is still unmet as written.

Worth carrying into the fix: the hint that error prints -- 'the task's status must match one of backlog/config.yml's statuses: exactly' -- is the LCLI-503 defect firing on a quest-backed workspace, i.e. the first thing a newly-added CI job would print would point a reader at a file this repo does not have. Landing LCLI-503 before or with this job is what keeps the new gate's failure output actionable.

THE FIRST CI GREEN WAS GREEN FOR THE WRONG REASON, and the gate would have shipped broken. Recorded because the tick said pass and only the log said why.

Clean-tree run 34990665392 on 3f697762: docs-gate PASS, 'bun run src/cli.ts check', '78 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, 9 out-of-bundle links skipped', whole run success after re-running an unrelated webkit flake. Every criterion I had written was satisfied.

But the log also said 'Declared Quest version: 0.6.0'. The job derives its Quest version from CLAUDE.md's managed block, as the Tracker integrity job does, and that block declared 0.6.0 while the fleet runs 0.7.0. quest 0.6.0's pausedStatus IS 'Blocked' -- the literal LCLI-333 carries. So CI classified the record happily and would have done so with or without the override.

Measured on one tree rather than argued:

  quest 0.7.0 (installed, fleet-current), no override  -> exit 6
  quest 0.6.0 (what CI installed), no override         -> exit 0
  quest 0.7.0, with override                           -> exit 0

The gate was therefore passing a bundle that fails on any current workstation, and WOULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT THE RED THIS TASK EXISTS FOR. It would have shipped as a working gate and been believed, because it agreed with the expectation -- the identical shape as opum-cli-e2e TASK-69's always-red job, arrived at from the opposite direction. Theirs was red for the wrong reason; this was green for the wrong reason. Neither is visible from the conclusion alone.

FIXED HERE: regenerated the managed block with 'quest agents --update-instructions --target claude' (one generated line, 0.6.0 -> 0.7.0, a routine write under the 2026-09-11 ruling). CI now installs the quest the fleet actually runs, so the docs gate exercises the real rename and the override is load-bearing rather than decorative. Verified after the bump: agents --check exits 0, lore check exits 0, full suite 3061 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail, lint and typecheck 0.

THE STRUCTURAL HALF IS NOT FIXED and is filed as LCLI-508: the Tracker integrity job installs the declared version and then checks the block against that same version, so it is self-consistent by construction and can never notice the declaration has fallen behind published quest. The one gate positioned to see it is the one that cannot. This instance is repaired; the next quest publish recreates it.

THE PROCEDURAL LESSON, worth more than either fix: the fleet's new two-sided rule says run the gate against a violation and against a clean tree. Both of my runs would have been correct-looking here. What actually caught it was reading the job log for WHICH VERSIONS the gate resolved, not just its exit code. A gate proof should include the versions the gate resolved, because two gates with identical exit codes can be measuring different things.

SESSION HANDOFF, 2026-09-15 — recycled over the fleet context budget, not blocked. PR #107 is open, everything is pushed, the working tree is clean at 8d24803a.

=== STATE, VERIFIED, NOT REMEMBERED ===

Branch fix/LCLI-504-ci-runs-lore-check, tip 8d24803a, 0 uncommitted files, nothing unpushed. PR #107 targets dev.

The two-sided gate proof the fleet rule requires is COMPLETE. Three runs, all resolving quest 0.7.0:
  ACCEPT  d613e190  run 34991819837  docs-gate success; 78 files, 0 errors; every other job green or skipped
  REJECT  58a1d8bd  run 34993134596  docs-gate the ONLY failure; exit 6; 'error index.md [broken-link]: link "reference/no-such-document.md" ... is not in the bundle'; 78 files, 1 error; NO quest error in the log; all eleven other jobs success or skipped
  ACCEPT  8d24803a  run 34993784197  docs-gate completed success (run still finishing its other jobs at handoff time)

Exit 6 with a BUNDLE error and no quest error is the part that matters, not the red. Exit 3 means the tracker binary is absent — the failure that made opum-cli-e2e's equivalent job red on its revert too, shipping an always-red gate that read as working.

=== WHY NO ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IS CHECKED ===

All four are genuinely unmet AS REPO STATE, because PR #107 has not merged. dev still has none of this. Checking any of them now would be checking on faith.

  AC#1 the job runs on every PR — TRUE on the branch and proven; 'gates the merge' needs AC#4, so not yet
  AC#2 the [reconcile.overrides] entry with the reason recorded — DONE on the branch, not on dev
  AC#3 lore check exits 0 on dev — NO. dev is unchanged. It exits 0 on this branch.
  AC#4 added to dev's required status checks — NOT DONE, see below

=== NEXT ACTIONS, IN ORDER ===

1. Wait for run 34993784197 to complete, confirm every job green or skipped, then squash-merge PR #107.
2. Check AC#1, #2, #3 once dev carries it; re-run 'lore check' on dev to evidence AC#3 rather than inferring it.
3. AC#4: THE USER APPROVED THIS DIRECTLY via AskUserQuestion this session — add 'lore check (docs gate)' to dev's required contexts, taking it from four to five. Verify the rendered name BY CODEPOINT from a real run first: the two existing 'lint · typecheck · test (...)' contexts carry U+00B7, not ASCII periods. The new name was deliberately chosen pure-ASCII so it cannot repeat that. Measured contexts on dev today: 'docker e2e harness (real lore + backlog binaries)', 'lint · typecheck · test (windows-latest)', 'Tracker integrity', 'lint · typecheck · test (ubuntu-latest)'.
4. THEN the LCLI-333 repair, which is now unblocked: quest 0.7.1 published (verified independently on npm, version 0.7.1, dist.integrity sha512-rSoY261euR4gHyKVNRZ+c1y/50vKpxnE7pYfaJAhcxzABlq8wOAjdJaHBChre2RmClU9+RCXhlOVW705cZEwBg==). quest-cli's QCLI-302 restores 'task start' on a record stranded at the retired literal. Install 0.7.1, 'quest doctor --json' names LCLI-333, then 'task start' and optionally 'task pause' to park it at 'Paused' — which is its honest state, held for wave 3. Then DELETE the [reconcile.overrides] entry, its header paragraph in .lore/config.toml, and the matching expectation in test/config.test.ts. The drift guard there exists to make that removal loud; do not leave it behind classifying a literal no conformant quest can emit.

It was deliberately NOT done in this PR: it would have invalidated an in-flight proof measurement for a change that is observably identical either way, since the override was built to produce the same rollup the repaired record will.

=== THINGS THAT WILL COST THE NEXT SESSION IF UNKNOWN ===

CI sets concurrency cancel-in-progress for pull_request. Pushing a new commit cancels the in-flight run. A gate proof needs its runs SERIALISED; racing them silently yields a one-sided proof that looks complete. 'gh run rerun <id> --failed' reuses the run and is safe.

A violation commit must contain ONLY the violation. 'git add -A' swept an unrelated LCLI-507 note into 58a1d8bd this session, so reverting it also reverted the note (restored in 8d24803a). It did not affect the measurement, but a violation commit carrying anything else has more than one candidate explanation for its red.

Four CI flakes hit this branch. All four were judged by whether the diff could reach the failing test, never by platform or test name, and all four cleared on re-run. See LCLI-507, which now carries a likely root cause and a defect in the guard that already exists for it.

=== FILED THIS SESSION, ALL To Do ===
LCLI-506 ADR-0009 still names backlog/config.yml as the status-vocabulary source; nothing supersedes it.
LCLI-507 init-wizard and friends time out in CI; four occurrences; the existing Bun-epoll retry is keyed only on the EEXIST string and misses the hang (exit 124).
LCLI-508 (HIGH) nothing detects that CLAUDE.md's declared Quest version has fallen behind published quest. This is the one that nearly shipped a meaningless gate — CI was resolving 0.6.0, whose pausedStatus IS 'Blocked', so the gate passed a bundle that fails on any current workstation.

Session write at 2026-09-15T16:16:20Z. Branch fix/LCLI-504-ci-runs-lore-check, 1 uncommitted file(s). Written by the opum-workflow write hook (0.7.4 (/Users/jdnewhouse/.claude/plugins/cache/opum-fleet/opum-workflow/0.7.4)), not by the model.

Correction to the handoff note above, made minutes later: run 34993784197 (the ACCEPT re-measurement on 8d24803a) has now COMPLETED — conclusion success, every job green or skipped, not just docs-gate. The handoff note recorded it as 'still finishing its other jobs', which was true when written.

So all three measurements are complete and each had every other job green or skipped on its own SHA, which is the half of the fleet rule that says the gate moved for its own reason rather than because something general broke.

The handoff commit itself (cf39f4aa) adds only this task record, so it starts one further run. That run — not 34993784197 — is the one to confirm green before merging PR #107, because it is the tree that will actually merge.

CLOSED OUT, 2026-09-15, with every criterion evidenced against dev or the live ruleset rather than inferred from the branch.

AC#1 — the job is on dev. PR #107 squash-merged at 6f5fa1b2 on run 34994183511 (head 02a087aa): completed/success, eleven jobs success and the two promotion guards skipped, "lore check (docs gate)" among them. "Gates the merge" is AC#4 below, not this line alone.

AC#2 — resolved twice over. The [reconcile.overrides] route landed on dev with #107 and satisfies the criterion as written. The stronger form follows in PR #108: quest 0.7.1 restores `task start` on a record stranded at the retired literal, `quest doctor --json` names LCLI-333 with code task_status_off_flow and prints the remedy, and `task start` then `task pause` moved it to "Paused" — its honest state, held for wave 3. The override, its committed header paragraph, and the drift guard in test/config.test.ts are all deleted there, because a stand-in that outlives the thing it stands in for goes on classifying a literal no conformant quest can emit.

AC#3 — measured on dev at 6f5fa1b2 with quest 0.7.1 installed: `lore check` exit 0, 78 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, 9 out-of-bundle links skipped. Re-measured with the override REMOVED on PR #108's tree: exit 0 again, identical counts. So the green is the record's own, not the override's.

AC#4 — ruleset require-ci-on-dev (id 22838594) now requires five contexts, up from four. The stored string was verified codepoint-by-codepoint against the rendered job name from run 34994183511 before it was written, and read back from `rules/branches/dev` after: 'lore check (docs gate)', every codepoint <= 0x7e. That check matters because two of the four pre-existing contexts carry U+00B7 rather than an ASCII period, and a context that does not match by rendered name is absent rather than red — which blocks dev until an admin notices. The user approved this ruleset change directly, twice: once in the previous session, and again here after I declined to act on the tracker note alone.

WHAT THE LIVE PROOF IS. PR #108 is the first pull request that has to satisfy the new required context, so its own required-check list — not this note — is the evidence that the gate blocks rather than merely reports.

ONE PROCESS NOTE WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX. The merge of #107 was refused by this session's own permission layer, not by a ruleset or a red check. That is the second time in this task that a conclusion and its reason came apart: the first was a docs gate that went green because CI had resolved quest 0.6.0. Both were only visible by reading past the verdict to what produced it.
finalSummary:
The repo's stated docs gate now exists, runs on every PR, and blocks.

A CI job "lore check (docs gate)" runs `lore check` from source against a real quest install, landed in PR #107 (squash 6f5fa1b2) with a two-sided proof: accept on d613e190 and 8d24803a, reject on 58a1d8bd with exit 6, a broken-link bundle error and no quest error in the log — the distinction that separates a working gate from the always-red one opum-cli-e2e shipped. It is now the fifth required context on dev's require-ci-on-dev ruleset, its name verified codepoint-by-codepoint because two existing contexts carry U+00B7.

The red the gate existed to catch is repaired at the source rather than papered over. LCLI-333 sat at "Blocked", the paused status quest 0.7.0 renamed and then could not move records off; quest 0.7.1 unstrands it, and PR #108 moves it to "Paused" and deletes the temporary [reconcile.overrides] entry, its header paragraph and its drift guard together. `lore check` exits 0 on dev with the override and without it.

The most valuable thing found here was not in scope: the first clean-tree run went green while CI was resolving quest 0.6.0, whose pausedStatus IS the retired literal — a gate that would have shipped as working and been believed, because it agreed with the expectation. Nothing could have caught it, and the structural reason is filed as LCLI-508: the one job positioned to notice the declaration has fallen behind published quest installs the declared version first and checks the block against that same version. PR #108 repairs this instance (0.7.0 -> 0.7.1); LCLI-508 stays open for the mechanism.
